# Supported UI behaviour matrix

<!-- generated by `quantick-app --dump-ui-behaviour-matrix`; do not edit -->

Every behaviour a trader can reach from the interface, and either the
control-plane capability that performs it or the recorded reason none
does. `CLAUDE.md`'s *Operable without a hand* is the rule this answers:
no capability ships reachable by mouse alone.

This file is generated; a hand edit is a guard failure, not a
correction. To change a row, change the table and regenerate:

```sh
cargo run -p quantick-app -- --dump-ui-behaviour-matrix \
  > docs/control-plane/ui-behaviour-matrix.md
```

The rows live one file per family under
`crates/operability/src/registry/`, joined by `FAMILIES` in
`registry.rs`; the guard that compares them against the interface
and against the capability registry lives beside them, and runs as
`cargo test -p quantick-app operability`.

**Reach** names every door into the behaviour — a toolbar button, a menu
entry and a hotkey are three doors into one room, and the row is the
room. **Capability** is the identifier an operator invokes, from
[the capability inventory](capability-inventory.md); more than one where
the control plane splits what the interface joins. **Exclusion** is the
class and the reason where no capability performs it.

The three exclusion classes are closed:

- `authority` — a ceiling refuses it on purpose. The reason cites the
  ceiling, and "why not add it" is answered there.
- `ui_only_by_decision` — an explicit product decision that the gesture
  stays the trader's. The reason cites where that decision is written.
- `pending_capability` — nothing refuses it and nobody has built it. The
  only class that is a debt, and every row in it is tracked in
  https://github.com/milocaetano/quantick/issues/401.

## Coverage

| Outcome | Behaviours |
| --- | --- |
| Reachable by capability | 127 |
| Excluded: `authority` | 4 |
| Excluded: `ui_only_by_decision` | 7 |
| Excluded: `pending_capability` | 43 |
| **Total** | **181** |

99 of the 181 rows claim at least one registry entry, so the drift guard fails when the interface changes under them. The other 82 say in the table that no registry stands behind them — a drag on a splitter, a number typed into the ticket — each with the reason, listed in full below. A row that says neither is a guard failure, not a third category.

| `home.show` | Show the Home tab | first tab of the market title strip, Ctrl+1, Ctrl+Shift+H | `home.show` | — |

## Appendix: rows no registry stands behind

A behaviour a trader names and no registry registers — a gesture drawn
straight onto a pane, a field inside a panel. The mechanical guard
cannot hold these up, so each says why in the table itself rather than
being counted and left anonymous. A row that claims no entry *and*
declares nothing here is a guard failure.

| Behaviour | Why nothing registers it |
| --- | --- |
| `layout.window.state.set` | native title-strip minimize/maximize buttons and free-space double-click |
| `home.leave` | market chip click and tab cycling while Home shows |
| `window.move` | native title-strip drag and window-edge resize gestures |
| `window.snap` | native Windows snapping |
| `app.exit` | native window close button |
| `tab.market.transfer` | native market-tab drag and insertion marker |
| `tab.market.drag.cancel` | native market-tab staged gesture and Escape |
| `window.close_preserving_tabs` | native close-to-survivor lifecycle |
| `market.palette.choose` | palette rows are drawn from the headless market list, not an action enum |
| `market.palette.add` | the no-match row is drawn from the headless market list |
| `market.palette.remove` | the row is drawn from the headless market list |
| `tab.market.roll` | the roll row is drawn from the headless market list, not an action enum |
| `chart.bars.set_spec` | the bar-kind and size controls are pane header widgets, not entries in an action enum |
| `chart.pan` | a pointer drag the canvas handles directly; no registry names it |
| `chart.price_axis.set` | price-axis gestures update the pane's PriceView directly |

## Appendix: registry entries that are not behaviours

Entries the guard sees and no row claims, because a row would be a
lie: a submenu that holds other entries and performs nothing itself, a
capture hook that opens a menu, a "nothing was clicked" variant. Each
carries its reason so a reader who disagrees has something to
disagree with.

| Source | Entry | Why not a behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `menu_entry` | `Help` | a submenu of the window menu; it holds entries and performs nothing |
| `menu_entry` | `Panels` | a submenu of the window menu; it holds entries and performs nothing |
| `menu_entry` | `Desk` | a submenu of the window menu; it holds entries and performs nothing |
| `menu_entry` | `Layouts` | a submenu holding the layout tabs and the three edits the strip's own menu holds; each of those is a row of its own |
| `rail_tool` | `Drawing` | the rail's slot for the drawing registry rather than a tool of its own; every drawing tool behind it is a `tool.*` row |
| `notice_action` | `None` | the feed notice's "nothing was clicked" variant: an absence, not a behaviour |
| `scripted_menu` | `window` | a capture hook that opens the window menu so a screenshot can see it. It performs nothing the menu's own entries do not |
| `scripted_menu` | `history` | a capture hook that opens the toolbar's history caret. The behaviour behind it is `history.reach.set` |
| `scripted_menu` | `theme` | a capture hook opening the native Theme menu; appearance.apply owns its choices |
| `scripted_menu` | `theme-dark` | a scripted native Dark click; appearance.apply owns the same publication |
| `scripted_menu` | `theme-light` | a scripted native Light click; appearance.apply owns the same publication |

11 entries.
